name: virtual-list
description: Renders only the rows inside the viewport, so list length costs no extra DOM

meta.name: VirtualList
meta.description: Renders only the rows inside the viewport, so list length costs no extra DOM

props.name: items
props.description: The full collection; only the visible window is rendered

props.name: itemHeight
props.description: Fixed row height in px — every row must be this tall

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the scrolling viewport, in px — not a CSS length, because the visible row count is computed from it

props.name: overscan
props.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the visible window, to cover fast scrolling.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible label for the list; label it when the list stands alone

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element.

whenToUse: Lists long enough that rendering every row costs noticeable time or memory (roughly a thousand rows and up)
Log, result and feed views where the collection is already fully in memory
Any list whose length is unbounded and rows are a uniform height
whenNotToUse: Short lists — the machinery costs more than it saves; use List
Rows of varying height, which this component cannot position without measuring
Content that must be findable with the browser’s in-page search, which cannot see unrendered rows

antiPatterns.bad: Passing rows whose real height differs from `itemHeight`
antiPatterns.good: Fix the row height in CSS to match `itemHeight` exactly
antiPatterns.why: Positions are arithmetic, not measured, so a mismatch makes rows overlap or leave gaps that grow with scroll depth

antiPatterns.bad: Reaching for a percentage or `dvh` viewport height
antiPatterns.good: Measure the container and pass a px number
antiPatterns.why: `height` drives the visible row count, which cannot be derived from a relative length without measuring

antiPatterns.good: Pair with InfiniteScroll, or load before passing `items`
antiPatterns.why: renderItem runs for every row entering the window, including on scroll-back, so a fetch there fires repeatedly

related.name: List
related.reason: Plain list when the collection is small enough to render whole

related.name: InfiniteScroll
related.reason: Loads further pages into the collection this list renders

related.name: DataTable
related.reason: Columnar data with sorting and selection rather than a flat row list

intent.a11yRationale: The viewport is a role="list" and each rendered row is a role="listitem" carrying aria-setsize and aria-posinset for the entire collection, so assistive technology announces "row 3 of 10000" rather than the size of the rendered window — the defect that makes naive virtualization unusable with a screen reader. The viewport is also in the tab order, because rows hold plain content rather than focusable controls and a scroll container with nothing focusable inside it is otherwise unreachable without a pointer; once focused it takes the browser’s native arrow, Page and Home/End scrolling. Rows are placed with transform rather than by mutating layout, so scrolling stays on the compositor. Because unrendered rows are absent from the DOM, browser in-page search cannot reach them; provide a real filter or search control alongside any virtualized list, and prefer a non-virtualized list when the collection is small.

flexibility.note: Fixed and uniform — variable row heights are not supported
